claims.claim_ar: فعل «اشْتَرَى» استخدام استعاري (مجاز/استعارة): اشتُقّ بمعنى أخذ النفس والمال كنوع من التفاني والتخصيص لله، فلا المراد شراء بالمعنى التجاري الحرفي بل استعارة للدلالة على التخصيص والتفاني.
claims.claim_en: The verb "اشترى" is used metaphorically (istiarah/majaz): 'bought' stands for taking/dedication of selves and wealth to God — not a literal commercial purchase but a metaphor indicating dedication/sacrifice.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Conveys a compact, powerful metaphor that frames believers' self-giving and spending as a solemn divine 'transaction', heightening the sense of committed sacrifice.

claims.claim_ar: الفعل «فاستبشروا» مأمور به على نحو الالتفات/الخطاب المباشر بعد سرد خبرى (إنَّ الله اشترى...)؛ أي تحويل الخطاب إلى مخاطبة مباشرة تدعو إلى الفرح والاطمئنان.
claims.claim_en: The verb "فاستبشروا" functions as an iltifat (shift/turn of address): after the report ("Indeed Allah has bought..."), the address shifts to a direct imperative/exhortation, inviting the listeners to rejoice and be reassured.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates immediacy and emotional engagement by shifting from a doctrinal statement to a direct exhortation, turning information into practical consolation.

claims.claim_ar: تواتر الأفعال «يُقَاتِلُونَ ... فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ» يظهر مقابلة وتوازيًا بلاغيًا (مرايا فعلية وصيغ مبالغة/مضارع)، يقوّي موضوع التضحية والجهاد عبر تركيب متوازن.
claims.claim_en: The sequence "يُقَاتِلُونَ ... فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ" exhibits muqabalah (balanced/paired structure): verbs are arranged in parallel/mirror fashion to reinforce the theme of sacrifice and combat.
claims.needs_review_reason: Supported by the commentary's use of the term 'مقابلة' in general, but the specific commentary excerpt does not explicitly analyze these exact verbs; further source linkage would strengthen confidence.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Emphasizes the reciprocity and totality of devotion (active fighting, being killed, and killing) by parallel verb forms, producing rhythmic and semantic reinforcement.
